producer_report.summary: The reader brief now has an "Enabled roles" section built from the effective config. A new prose-only tenth reading rule says brief content targets only enabled roles. Root cause: the reader was never told which roles run, so it wrote planner/critic content although [job_plan] was off. `Config::enabled_roles` returns reader, producer and verifier always, and planner and critic only when [job_plan] is present and enabled (any mode). `read_once` passes that list in the new `ReaderInputs::enabled_roles` field. I ran the targeted tests, the boundary scan and the mirrors test. I did not run the full suite, clippy or `cargo fmt --check`; I ran `cargo fmt --all` once.

checks_run.note: 101 passed, including the two new brief tests and the updated rule-count test

criteria_check.criterion: A new unit test in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs builds a reader brief with job planning disabled and asserts the brief names reader, producer and verifier as enabled roles and does not list planner or critic as enabled; run `cargo test -p athena-context`.
criteria_check.evidence: Test the_reader_brief_lists_only_reader_producer_and_verifier_when_job_planning_is_off passed in `cargo test -p athena-context briefs` (101 passed).

criteria_check.criterion: A second test builds the brief with job planning enabled and asserts planner and critic appear in the enabled-roles section; run `cargo test -p athena-context`.
criteria_check.evidence: Test the_reader_brief_lists_planner_and_critic_when_job_planning_is_on passed in the same run.

criteria_check.criterion: A test in crates/athena-core (e.g. reading.rs tests) shows read_once/reader input construction derives the role list from the config's [job_plan] enabled value, not a hard-coded list; run `cargo test -p athena-core`.
criteria_check.evidence: reading.rs test the_reader_input_roles_come_from_the_config_job_plan_enabled_value passed. It toggles the shipped config's job_plan.enabled and sets job_plan to None, then checks the roles. It also checks that the source contains `enabled_roles: jc.config.enabled_roles(),`. I ran only that test, not the whole athena-core suite. A separate athena-data test, enabled_roles_follow_the_job_plan_enabled_value, also passed.

criteria_check.criterion: crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs READING_RULES contains a new rule stating that brief content targets only enabled roles, marked `(prose only)`, and the array length and existing length assertions are updated consistently.
criteria_check.evidence: READING_RULES is now [&str; 10] and its last entry ends with `(prose only).`. The existing test asserts len == 10 and that the prose-only line exists. Its size cap is raised from 2750 to 2900 bytes. That test passed.

criteria_check.criterion: reader_brief output has a heading section listing the currently enabled roles, checkable by Grep of the heading constant in briefs.rs.
criteria_check.evidence: `ENABLED_ROLES_HEADING` ("# Enabled roles") is defined in briefs.rs and rendered by reader_brief before the reading rules. The new brief tests find the section by it.

criteria_check.criterion: No unrelated behavior changes: `cargo test` passes with all existing tests, `cargo clippy --all-targets` is clean, and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks. I ran the targeted tests, the boundary scan and the mirrors test, and `cargo fmt --all`.

mistakes: My first CHANGELOG edit failed because the match was not unique; I redid it with the `## [Unreleased]` heading included.
learnings: ReaderInputs is constructed in only two places: read_once in reading.rs and the reader_inputs test helper in briefs.rs.
JobPlanConfig is Copy, so Config methods can use `self.job_plan.is_some_and(|p| p.enabled)`.
